name: Lactitol + Ispaghula Husk
meta: Lactitol monohydrate + Ispaghula husk powder (90 g pack)
Prescription-only fixed-dose combination. Components – Lactitol: Non-prescription /
OTC category for this ingredient (combination may be Schedule H); Ispaghula (Psyllium) Husk: Non-prescription / OTC category for this ingredient (combination may be Schedule H)
sections: White crystalline powder; melting point 146 °C; available as anhydrous, monohydrate or dihydrate.
Not applicable – seed husk of Plantago ovata Forssk. (mucilage rich in arabinoxylan)
Pinkish-white to light-brown flakes or powder; swells to a gel with water.

Lactitol: A sugar alcohol derived from lactose; also used as a low-calorie sweetener. First approval/introduction: Used in Europe since the 1980s; US FDA February 2020 for chronic idiopathic constipation. Ispaghula (Psyllium) Husk: India (Gujarat) is the world's principal producer. The US FDA (1998) authorised a health claim that soluble fibre from psyllium may reduce the risk of heart disease by lowering cholesterol (≥7 g/day). First approval/introduction: Marketed in India since 1937; in the USA since 1934 (G. D. Searle).
Lactitol monohydrate + Ispaghula husk powder (90 g pack)
Lactitol softens stool osmotically and acts as a prebiotic; ispaghula adds bulk and normalises consistency – dual action with less bloating than higher doses of either.

Lactitol Non-absorbable disaccharide fermented by colonic bacteria to short-chain fatty acids, increasing osmotic pressure and stool water content; also acts as prebiotic. Receptor / target profile: Osmotic laxative and prebiotic (increases bifidobacteria and lactobacilli).

Ispaghula (Psyllium) Husk Hydrophilic mucilage absorbs water to form a gel, increasing stool bulk and softness and stimulating peristalsis; also normalises stool consistency in diarrhoea and lowers cholesterol. Receptor / target profile: Hydrophilic mucilage absorbs water, increases stool bulk and moisture, stimulates peristalsis and binds bile acids.
Colonic bacterial fermentation to short-chain fatty acids
Summary: Minimal absorption; metabolised by colonic flora.
Summary: Not absorbed; partially fermented in colon. Effect in 12–72 h.

Lactitol: Diarrhoea; correct fluids. Ispaghula (Psyllium) Husk: Obstruction risk if taken without fluid.
Lactitol comparable to lactulose for constipation and hepatic encephalopathy with better palatability (Blanc et al., meta-analysis 1992).
Ispaghula effective for chronic constipation (systematic reviews).

Store below 30°C in a dry place, protected from light and moisture. Keep out of the reach of children. Do not use after the expiry date.
